name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills district, a pine-covered hill station at about 1,500 m elevation known as the Scotland of the East. Colonial architecture, markets, lakes, and base for exploring Khasi Hills attractions.

name: Dawki / Umngot River
description: Border town and crystal-clear river in West Jaintia Hills on the India-Bangladesh frontier. The Umngot River is renowned as one of Asia’s cleanest, with transparent waters that make boats appear to float in mid-air during the dry season. Features the 1932 British-built suspension bridge and boating.
facts: Umngot River ~82 km long; origin near Shillong Peak
Dawki Suspension Bridge built 1932 by British
Best clarity November–March; Integrated Check Post to Bangladesh

name: Shnongpdeng
description: Riverside village and adventure hub about 8 km upstream from Dawki on the Umngot River. Popular for camping, kayaking, cliff jumping, swimming in clear waters, and quieter stretches away from the main border traffic. Emerging eco-tourism spot in West Jaintia Hills.
facts: Preferred for adventure activities and riverside camping
Clear water and sandy beaches in dry season

name: Krang Suri Falls
description: Stunning turquoise waterfall near Amlarem in West Jaintia Hills, plunging into a natural pool of brilliant blue-green water surrounded by forest. Popular for swimming (life jackets available), photography, and short trek to the base. One of Meghalaya’s most photogenic falls.
facts: Near Amlarem, ~30 km from Jowai, ~90 km from Shillong
Natural plunge pool with clear turquoise water
Entry fee applies; swimming with life jackets

name: Nartiang Monoliths
description: Largest collection of megaliths in the Khasi-Jaintia region, in Nartiang village (former summer capital of Jaintia kings). Features tall menhirs (moo shynrang) and dolmens (moo kynthai) erected from the 16th–19th centuries to commemorate royalty, warriors, and ancestors. Often called the Stonehenge of Northeast India.
facts: Erected by U Mar Phalyngki and clans between ~1500–1835
About 24–30 km from Jowai, 60 km from Shillong

name: Nartiang Durga Temple
description: Ancient temple dedicated to Goddess Durga (Jayanti Devi) in Nartiang, one of the 51 Shakti Peethas. Features unique tribal-style worship blending Hindu and local Jaintia traditions; over 500 years old and a major pilgrimage site during Durga Puja.
facts: Located in Nartiang near the monoliths
Unique fusion of Hindu and tribal worship

name: Thadlaskein Lake
description: Historic man-made lake near Mukhla on NH6, about 8–10 km from Jowai. According to legend, dug by 290 clans under rebel general Sajar Nangli using bow ends. Popular for boating, picnics, and scenic views; also known as Pung Sajar Nangli.
facts: About 58–70 km from Shillong, 8–10 km from Jowai
Legend of creation by Sajar Nangli’s clans

name: Jowai
description: District headquarters of West Jaintia Hills and cultural centre of the Pnar (Jaintia) people. Hill town at ~1,365–1,380 m elevation surrounded by the Myntdu River; gateway to Nartiang, Thadlaskein, Krang Suri and Dawki circuits, with markets, churches, and local cuisine.
facts: HQ of West Jaintia Hills district
Home to Pnar people; about 65 km from Shillong
Base for Jaintia Hills tourism circuit
